### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-core`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/rest`, touching **13** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/metadata-core/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**30** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 80a9f99222a62c336659bef6e8dcabd7ffb7b1b3`.

⛔ **11** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/metadata-core/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **212** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **34** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 80a9f99222a62c336659bef6e8dcabd7ffb7b1b3` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `e6c799ce6779b274e70e5e08e12bcd4cf5478d4f` — the merge of head `0b381cd7e53fee03d03f07f96f6fcbfe2ba7525f` into base `80a9f99222a62c336659bef6e8dcabd7ffb7b1b3`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin e6c799ce6779b274e70e5e08e12bcd4cf5478d4f && git checkout e6c799ce6779b274e70e5e08e12bcd4cf5478d4f
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 80a9f99222a62c336659bef6e8dcabd7ffb7b1b3 0b381cd7e53fee03d03f07f96f6fcbfe2ba7525f && git checkout -B drift-repro 80a9f99222a62c336659bef6e8dcabd7ffb7b1b3 && git merge --no-ff 0b381cd7e53fee03d03f07f96f6fcbfe2ba7525f

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 80a9f99222a62c336659bef6e8dcabd7ffb7b1b3
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 80a9f99222a62c336659bef6e8dcabd7ffb7b1b3` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

Head moved · 2026-10-31T19:45Z

The head is now `0b381cd7`, so the contract review claimed at `de1f609b` (2026-10-31T19:44Z) should be taken at `0b381cd7`. The new commit is test-only and lives in `@objectstack/service-automation`. Four flow `get_record` pins expected a `runAs:'user'` run to be served a capability-gated stored row. The PR's rule now withholds that row.

- The projection and keyed-hash pins now run under `runAs:'system'`.
- The user-identity cases now pin the other side of the rule: no row is served, and the run receives nothing from it.
- An ablation (gate removed) turns the three new pins red.
- The whole package passes: 244 files, 3105 tests.

**For the review: one narrowing this PR states.** A flow's user-identity run context carries permission-set names but no system capabilities. So a `runAs:'user'` flow is withheld gated stored rows, whoever triggered it. That fails closed and sits within the ruling's arm. Making a flow run aware of the caller's capabilities is out of this card's scope.

Contract-review-hold: head `de1f609b0f2bb9202ae3009d5ed22010a61d694c` is red · 2026-10-31T19:47Z

Claim 6548265017 stands; no record on this head (a PASS is never written on a red head).

- Read at this stamp: card #27884 (ruling A 6545628488, claim 6545739621, dev report 6547945667), the PR diff (12 files, +610/−13 against merge-base 630b4078, merge-tree clean), check-runs: 50 latest-per-name, 34 success + 14 skipped, 2 failed (Test Core, Test Core 8/8).
- The red: `@objectstack/service-automation` `pnpm run test` exited 1 — 4 tests in 2 files (job 124633119907): `src/builtin/get-record-stored-metadata-family.integration.test.ts` (3: the `runAs:'user'` findOne and find branches, and the crypto-provider case) and `src/builtin/get-record-stored-metadata-filter-refusal.integration.test.ts` L352 (`runAs:'user'`, scalar-column filter). Each reads the stored `datasource` row (`pin_flow_ds` / `pin_filter_ds`) as the triggering user and expects the projected body; under this PR a caller below datasource administration is served no row, so the CEL path `rec.metadata` finds no key, `rec[0]` is out of bounds, and `row` is null.
- Reading: the behaviour is the ruling (a flow `get_record` node is an exit that serves the document, and it now admits the readers the `/meta` door admits). The pins are stale, not the gate: the `runAs:'user'` cases become "served no row" pins (or run as a holder of `manage_platform_settings`), and their control is a system-context door read, so "like the door" for a `runAs:'user'` run is now "no row". The `runAs:'system'` cases keep their shape.
- Outside the PR's own sweep: the body's suite list names objectql, metadata-core, rest and the dogfood battery; `service-automation` is a sibling reader of the family that the derived gates do not run. Worth naming in the next dev report's tests line.
- Contract content otherwise reads clean: one table in `@objectstack/metadata-core`, the same frozen object at the rest exit (parity pin), the engine gate registered in the constructor on both family tables with `isSystem` and context-less reads exempt, the event arm fail-closed for every subscriber, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` + `Metadata-protocol: none` + the ADR-0087 `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` marker on a `!` title (Check Changeset green), three patch bumps. The record follows on the next green head, with the delta from `de1f609b`.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `0b381cd7e53fee03d03f07f96f6fcbfe2ba7525f`
Local-runs: none
Scope: PR #28465 (Fixes #27884, ruling A 6545628488; claim 6545739621; dev report 6547945667), 14 files, +670/−20 against merge-base 630b4078, merge-tree clean. Hold 6548302963 on `de1f609b` (service-automation pins red); the delta `de1f609b` → `0b381cd7` is one commit, test-only (2 service-automation files, +60/−7): the three `runAs:'user'` family cases and the scalar-filter case become "served no row" pins (output null / `[]`, no sentinel and no configuration in the run), the `runAs:'system'` cases keep the projected-body shape, the crypto-provider case runs as system; no source file moved.
Inputs: card #27884 (triage 6513852880, decision letter 6538434026, rulings B 6522945866 then A 6545628488), the PR body and changeset, the full diff, `origin/main` for every cited symbol, check-runs (read 2026-10-31T20:16Z: all 50 latest-per-name check-runs completed, 38 success + 12 skipped, none failed, none running) — 50 checks

### ① Ruling → code
- Letter A: the stored-row read exit admits only readers holding the capability the `/meta` type gate names for the type; the same row at the one other exit; event exits withhold the body; admins and system reads unchanged; the save-door half of B dropped. The diff is exactly that: `STORED_METADATA_TYPE_READ_CAPABILITIES` (`datasource`, `external_catalog` → `manage_platform_settings`) moves to `@objectstack/metadata-core` with `storedMetadataTypesWithheldFrom(caller)` and `isCapabilityGatedStoredMetadataType(type)`; `@objectstack/rest` `META_TYPE_READ_CAPABILITIES` is that same frozen object (parity pin `toBe`); the engine registers `storedMetadataTypeReadGate` in its constructor on `STORED_METADATA_BODY_OBJECTS` (`sys_metadata`, `sys_metadata_history`, the family's one definition in `@objectstack/spec/kernel`) and AND-composes `type $nin withheld` into `find` / `findOne` / `count` / `aggregate` for a caller lacking a row's capability; `redactEventMetadataBody` drops the body of a gated type for every subscriber (fail-closed arm).
- Admission predicate is the `/meta` gate's: `metaTypeReadRefusal` (main L2114) reads `systemPermissions.includes(capability)` with no `isSystem` arm and refuses an anonymous caller; `storedMetadataTypesWithheldFrom` withholds every listed type from a caller with no capability set. Same cohort at both exits, pinned for six callers.
- Exemptions match the posture every engine read gate takes: `isSystem` and context-less reads (loader, `/meta` store reads, boot) are not narrowed; census row 18d names `storedMetadataTypeReadFilter` as the `isSystem` exemption and the register table carries it.
- No save-door change, no spec change, no `protocol.ts` change, no new key or permission name: as the letter binds.

### ② Declarations
- `Clause-②: no (narrowing for readers below datasource administration)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` on the PR and in the changeset: right. No schema key moves; what narrows is the read set of a stored row. ADR-0087 marker `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` on the `!` title, Check Changeset green.
- Three patch bumps (metadata-core, objectql, rest): consistent with the family's read-gate precedent #21087 (a fix in rest/runtime).

### ③ Pins and ablations
- objectql: admin whole row; org-admin and plain reader served no gated row on all four reads (a get of the id answers null, not a refusal); history table by the same row; system read not narrowed; composed predicate exact; events of gated rows carry no body while an ungated row keeps it. rest: same frozen object; six-caller parity. Dogfood: booted stack, `organization_admin_no_bypass` holder and a plain member served nothing on list / query / get, metadata door 403, per-caller parity data-door ⇔ meta-door. The body records five ablations each red then restored.
- `engine-realtime-stored-metadata-body.test.ts` re-pinned from "projected datasource body" to "withheld whole", with the ungated case moved to a `view` row: the #21120 pin's intent (no credential on the wire) still holds, strengthened.
- The `de1f609b` red (four `runAs:'user'` flow `get_record` pins in service-automation expecting a projected datasource row for a reader below datasource administration) is fixed on this head by re-pinning those four cases to "served no row" (both family tables, both node branches) and keeping the projected-body pins on `runAs:'system'`; Test Core 8/8 green.

### ④ Traps and should-fix
- A flow `get_record` node is an exit that serves the document: under A a `runAs:'user'` run below datasource administration is served no row, which the fixed pins now state. `runAs:'system'` runs keep the projected body.
- A list for the next card on the family: the derived gates do not run sibling readers' suites (service-automation here); the dev report's tests line should name them.
SHOULD_is fixed on this head by re-pinning those four cases to "served no row" (both family tables, both node branches) and keeping the projected-body pins on `runAs:'system'`; Test Core 8/8 green.

- 为什么改：你在 15:47 对批次 #433 的「同意」（裁定 A）。
- 风险与回滚：这是收窄。以用户身份运行（runAs:'user'）的流程也读不到这类行，属于故障时关闭（fail-closed）。需要读取的调用方授予 `manage_platform_settings` 即可。回滚即 revert。

### ⛔ merge queue 构建失败 — 先分诊，再决定要不要重排

队列构建 [41239207302](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/actions/runs/41239207302) 红了。队列跑的是**全量**套件（PR 侧 CI 只跑 affected 子集），
所以失败的测试可能在本 PR 没碰过的包里 —— 那不是重排能修的。每次盲目重排都会让排在后面的所有 PR 重建一轮。

**分类：`failure`** —— 按下面的日志分诊。

**失败的 job（日志抽取，best effort）：**

- **[Live E2E UI](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/actions/runs/41239207302/job/124649443030)** — 失败步骤: Run the live e2e specs（日志不可读，点进 job 看）

> `↳ 失败原因` 是判读的关键：**超时**（`Test timed out in …` / `Hook timed out in …`）多半是负载/时序，不是本 PR 的回归；
> **断言**（`AssertionError: …`）才指向真实的行为改变。两者的 `FAIL` 行长得一模一样，只有这一行能区分。
>
> ⚠️ **断言这一侧有一类例外，判据是断言在测什么，不是它是不是 `AssertionError`。** 断言的对象是**产品行为**（一个值、一个形状、一次拒收）⇒ 照上面读：真实的行为改变，去查，⛔ 不要重排掉；
> 断言的对象是**这次实验自身的有效性前提**（跑完的耗时、负载下的先后、任何只在时间预算内才成立的条件）⇒ 它跟**超时**是同一类，同样对负载敏感，重排一次是合法的判别手段。
> 识别是机械的：断言的消息或它比较的值本身点名了一段**时长、一个时间戳、一个耗时计数**。实测过的一对 —— `AssertionError: SecurityPlugin.init() ran: expected false to be true` 测的是产品行为（真回归）；
> `AssertionError: this run took over a second, so second-precision stamps could have differed too: expected 1006 to be less than 1000` 测的是实验前提：它守护的那条不变式当时是绿的，同一个 head 原样重排一次即成功。
> 穿着 `AssertionError` 外衣的时间测量，仍然是时间测量。（⛔ 这只改「怎么读一次红」，不改「哪些测试可以重排」——后者由别处管。）

**跨 PR 相同签名（24h，按失败测试文件聚合）：**

- ⚠️ **本次没有可用的聚合签名**（日志里没有能解析出测试文件名的 FAIL 行）—— 这不是「没有同签名的其他 PR」，是**这一轮没测到**。跨 PR 聚合本次不可用，请手工比对其他 PR 的同类评论。
- ⚠️ 24h 评论账本**没读完**（超过 5 页仍未读到窗口尽头），所以上面的「不同 PR 数」是**下界**，不是全量。

- 本 PR 过去 24h 无队列失败记录（首次）。
- 过去 24h 队列共有 2 个失败构建（不含本次）。

1. 失败测试在本 PR 改动的包里 → 真回归，修 PR。
2. 失败测试与本 PR 无关 → 看上面的「跨 PR 相同签名」；已有汇总 issue ⇒ flaky/环境问题实锤，去那张 issue 上谈，修好前重排只会再烧一轮全队列。
